references.text: Repeats the theme of sevenfold punishment for disobedience; the same expression 'שֶׁבַע' (seven) is used to describe the intensity of God's discipline.
Continues the pattern of sevenfold punishment as a consequence of not listening to God.
Concludes the series with sevenfold discipline, showing God's progressive correction.
Parallel warning about the consequences of not listening to the Lord's voice and keeping His commandments.
Describes God's discipline (יָסַר/מוּסָר) as an expression of love, using the same root as 'לְיַסְּרָה' in Leviticus.
The prophet Amos describes how Israel did not return to God despite His discipline.
Jeremiah laments that the people refused to accept discipline (מוּסָר) and turn back.
Isaiah describes a people who continue in rebellion despite repeated discipline.
Hebrews quotes Proverbs and explains that the Lord's discipline is a sign of His love for His children.
Jesus says that He rebukes and disciplines those He loves, and calls them to repentance.
